BG.thesis_one_line: World's largest grain and oilseed processor, earning more after merging with Viterra, but the price already assumes good times last and cash flow is negative.
key_adverse_facts: Trailing free cash flow about -$711M (TTM operating cash flow about $1,075M less capex about $1,786M, my arithmetic from 10-Q/10-K); H1-26 operating cash flow -$1,126M
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance $9.25-9.75 vs FY25 adjusted $7.57 and FY24 $9.19; Q1-26 gross margin fell to 3.5% from 5.1%; Q2 GAAP EPS $3.47 includes a $1.67 mark-to-market gain versus adjusted $2.00
Brazil PIS/COFINS tax claims outstanding $598M at 2026-06-30, up from $490M at 2025-12-31 (10-Q), not accrued
Consolidated debt $15,214M (net $14,621M); only about $1.3B after $13,311M readily marketable inventories; net interest guided $620-660M
data_conflicts: Triage Q02 quoted net debt/EBITDA 5.2x and FCF yield -30.9%; filings give consolidated net debt $14.6B (about $1.3B after RMI) and TTM FCF about -3.4% of market cap
Headline 88% revenue growth is Viterra merger-driven, not organic
BG.confidence_in_thesis: med: business and 2026 earnings are well evidenced; mid-cycle margin and cash conversion are the open questions

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Reverse DCF (9.5% cost of equity, FCF/share $6.18 = 65% of FY26 EPS midpoint) implies 5.0% 10-year growth vs my base 3% (worth about $94 vs price $109).

BG.scenario_basis: FY29 adjusted EPS 6.7/9.83/13.1 (bear/base/bull) x exit P/E 9/11/12.5 from $109; dividends $2.88-3.15 a year; base 178M shares after buybacks.
kill_criteria: Company cuts the FY26 adjusted EPS guidance below $9.00 at the low end, or reports adjusted EPS below $1.50 in two consecutive quarters (Q1-26 $1.83, Q2-26 $2.00).
Consolidated debt (short-term debt + current portion + long-term debt, 10-Q balance sheet) less cash less RMI (10-Q RMI note) exceeds $4.0B at any quarter-end (2026-06-30: about $1.3B).
S&P long-term rating below BBB+ or Moody's below Baa2 (currently A- and Baa1).
Trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow minus capex (10-Q/10-K cash flow statement) below -$1.5B at two consecutive quarter-ends (2026-06-30: about -$0.7B).
Brazil PIS/COFINS outstanding claims in the 10-Q contingencies note exceed $1.0B (2026-06-30: $598M).

IFF.thesis_one_line: Maker of flavours and fragrances selling its food-ingredients arm to cut debt, but growth is modest and the price assumes much faster cash growth.
key_adverse_facts: FY25 free cash flow only $256M on adjusted EPS ex amortization $4.20; FY25 GAAP EPS $(1.46) after $1,153M goodwill impairment in H1-25
Open EC, UK CMA, Swiss, Mexican, Singapore and India fragrance investigations; provisions recognised but undisclosed; 10-Q says outcome could have a material adverse effect
Goodwill $8,145M and intangibles $3,732M are about 85% of equity $14,009M

Food Ingredients sale (about $4.3B, net proceeds about $3.8B) not closed; outside date 2027-05-28; EUR 800M notes due 2026-09-25 refinanced via a $1.0B term loan undrawn at June 30, draw status unverified
Like-for-like EBITDA guidance top end drifted about $30M lower after re-basing (my arithmetic: $2.05-2.12B vs $2.05-2.15B)
data_conflicts: Triage Q13 quoted negative TTM margin/ROE and FCF yield -7.9%: driven by the H1-25 impairment and discontinued-ops perimeter; continuing ops H1-26 EPS $0.73 GAAP
Quarterly rows are on different perimeters (Q3-25 to Q1-26 include Food Ingredients; Q2-26 is continuing operations)
Whether the September 25 2026 note maturity was refinanced through the term loan draw was not found in filings opened
IFF.confidence_in_thesis: low-med: portfolio change is clear, but pro forma free cash flow is my estimate and investigations are unresolved

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Reverse DCF (8.5% cost of equity, pro forma FCF/share $2.74) implies 10.4% 10-year growth (7.1% on optimistic $795M FCF) vs my base 8% for 3 years then 4% worth about $59.

IFF.scenario_basis: FY29 pro forma FCF/share 2.30/3.46/4.40 (bear/base/bull) at exit FCF yield 5.5%/4.5%/4.0% from $85.69; dividend $1.60 a year; base start FCF/share $2.74 (about $620M on 226M shares after $2.5B buyback).
kill_criteria: Company-stated net debt to credit-adjusted EBITDA (release debt-covenant table) above 3.25x at any quarter-end (2026-06-30: 2.5x; covenant maximum 3.75x).
The Food Ingredients sale is terminated, or has not closed by the May 28 2027 outside date (8-K acc. 0001193125-26-249963).
Continuing-operations adjusted operating EBITDA guidance cut below $1.53B, or comparable currency-neutral sales growth below 2% for two consecutive quarters (Q2-26: +6%).
Free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex, 10-Q) below $500M for the 12 months to the 2027-06-30 quarter (H1-26: $378M).
A fine or settlement above $250M in the European Commission, UK CMA, Swiss, Mexican, Singapore or India fragrance investigations (none quantified in the 10-Q; provisions recognised but undisclosed).

TRGP.thesis_one_line: Owns gas-processing, pipeline and export assets in the US's busiest oil basin and keeps beating forecasts, but the shares already price that success.
key_adverse_facts: Consolidated debt $19,578M (net about $19.45B, about 3.5x trailing adjusted EBITDA, my arithmetic); owners' equity only $3,796M
2026 funding gap: growth capex about $4.5B plus dividends about $1.07B exceed cash flow; H1-26 cash taxes $0.7M vs $680M 2026E tax expense, so cash taxes will rise as capex falls
Q2 raise attributed to strong marketing and optimization margin; realized Q2 gas price $(2.48)/MMBtu on negative Waha prices with producer curtailments
NMED proposed civil penalty about $47.8M (compliance order dated 2024-12-05) on Red Hills; MIECO $6.9M verdict before Texas Supreme Court certification (2026-07-24)
data_conflicts: Triage quoted 23.3x NTM P/E; guided 2026 GAAP net income $2,285M gives about 26x; triage 3.5x leverage is reproduced as consolidated net debt/TTM adjusted EBITDA
High ROE (triage 71%) reflects book equity of only $3.8B after buybacks and depreciation, not only profitability
Reverse-DCF 2028 free cash flow path is my assumption, not company guidance
TRGP.confidence_in_thesis: med: franchise and 2026 guidance well evidenced; 2028 free cash flow path and cash taxes are assumptions

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Reverse DCF (8.5% cost of equity; FCF/share 0.6/4.0/15.5 for 2026-28 then growth) implies 6.6% growth for 2029-35 (8.3% at 9%) vs my base 5% worth about $255 (8.5%) or $234 (9%).

TRGP.scenario_basis: 2029 adjusted EBITDA $6.3B/7.43B/8.0B at EV/EBITDA 9x/11x/12.5x from $277.84; net debt $22.5B/21.5B/20.5B; 212M shares base; dividends $5.0-7.0 a year.
kill_criteria: Consolidated net debt (10-Q: current debt obligations plus long-term debt less cash) divided by trailing four-quarter adjusted EBITDA above 4.0x at any quarter-end (2026-06-30: about 3.5x).
Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance cut below the $5.7B low end, or Q3 or Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA below $1.35B (Q2-26: $1,603M; Q4-25: $1,341M).
Any slip of Train 12, Train 13 or Speedway first-operation date beyond the dates in the company release (Speedway Q3 2027; Train 13 Q1 2028), or 2027 net growth capex guidance above $4.5B.
Permian natural gas inlet volumes fall year-over-year in any quarter, or realized Waha price negative for a full quarter again with producer curtailments cited in the release.
Final NMED penalty above $100M on the Red Hills matter (proposed approximately $47.8M in the December 5 2024 compliance order) or any other single environmental or litigation charge above $100M.
